notes.content:
Landed in c09a189 (gh-90). skrifa is wired as a PER-GLYPH second opinion and that part works,
but FontProgram::parse() still only succeeds when the PRIMARY decoder does. A font our own
glyph_truetype/glyph_cff reject outright therefore still falls to the advance box, even
though skrifa might read it fine.

CAUSE: select_gid() in font.rs resolves GIDs entirely against the primary decoder's own
encoding/charset tables (gid_for_code / is_cid_keyed / gid_for_cid) and has no skrifa-aware
path. Fixing it means editing font.rs, which was outside the implementing agent's owned
paths, so it was correctly left alone rather than reshaped underneath a file it did not own.

NOT urgent: does not affect the gh-67 ceilings (predefined-Expert CFF encoding, CID-keyed
CFF, seac) -- those fonts PARSE fine and fail on individual glyphs, which the per-glyph
fallback already covers. This is only about wholesale parse failure.

ALSO STILL UNPROVEN generally: we have no font sample that our decoders fail and skrifa
rescues, so the rescue path is wired but not demonstrated end-to-end. What would prove it:
a real embedded font hitting one of the gh-67 ceilings, run through
'annots --scan-fallback' before/after. The maintainer's test-annotation.pdf is NOT such a
sample -- it scans 0 fallback pages already.

title: kopitiam-pdf: skrifa cannot rescue a font our primary decoders reject entirely (parse() requires primary success)
